findings.target: Crucially, they declared the agreement void under Section 20 of the Indian Contract Act due to mutual mistake of fact regarding the Government's title to the subject matter
findings.question: Did the High Court declare the agreement void under Section 20 ICA?
findings.source_answer: Source S4da221281e65 states High Court held contract was made out but specific performance sought was not the contract entered into, and agreement was void under section 20 ICA due to mistake of fact as regards title. This is supported.

evidence.quote: agreement was void under cite15†section 20 of the Indian Contract Act, as both parties were under a mistake of fact as regards the title

findings.needed_change: No change needed for this specific inference if F1/F2 are fixed. However, check if 'title' vs 'competence' distinction matters. Source says 'title'. Draft says 'title'. OK.

findings.target: The attempt to seek compensation or alternative relief failed because the Lime Co. did not strictly adhere to the requirements of Section 15 of the Specific Relief Act, specifically the relinquishment of all claims for deficiency or damages for prior periods
findings.question: Did the Lime Co. actually fail to relinquish claims, or did they make an application doing so?
findings.original_answer: Failed because did not strictly adhere/relinquish.
findings.source_answer: Source S952f65c826eb says High Court disallowed claim because application dated Feb 18, 1952 did not show relinquishment. But Source S7093796118f1 quotes an application claiming relief under Sec 15 AND relinquishing claims for period prior to April 1, 1948. The conflict is whether the *pleaded* case matched the *statutory* requirement. The draft omits that the Lime Co. *did* file an application attempting to relinquish, but the HC found it insufficient or inconsistent with the suit's main prayer.

evidence.quote: He further relinquishes all claims to further performance and all right to compensation either for the deficiency or for the loss or damages sustained by him for default of the defendant for the period prior to 1st April, 1948.

findings.needed_change: Clarify that while the Lime Co. filed an application purporting to relinquish claims (S7093796118f1), the High Court held the conditions of Section 15 were not fulfilled (S952f65c826eb), possibly due to inconsistency with the main suit or timing.
